# terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator { #formulae.terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator }

```python
terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator(op, *args)
```

Deferred unary or binary operation.

Functions calls like `a + b` are converted into a LazyOperator that is resolved when you
explicitly evaluates it.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**op**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[builtin_function_or_method](`builtin_function_or_method`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   An operator in the `operator` built-in module. It can be one of `add`, `pos`, `sub`, `neg`, `pow`, `mul`, and `truediv`.

<code>[**args**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [()]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   One or two lazy instances.

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [eval](#formulae.terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator.eval) | Evaluates the operation. |

### eval { #formulae.terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator.eval }

```python
terms.call_resolver.LazyOperator.eval(data_mask, env)
```

Evaluates the operation.

Evaluates the arguments involved in the operation, calls the Python operator, and returns
the result.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**data_mask**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pd](`pd`).[DataFrame](`pd.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The data frame where variables are taken from

<code>[**env**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Environment](`Environment`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The environment where values and functions are taken from.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[**result**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The value obtained from the operator call.
